item_a.claimed_date: 196 BCE (Ptolemaic Period, reign of Ptolemy V Epiphanes)
item_a.claimed_material: Granodiorite stele inscribed with three scripts: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic script, and Ancient Greek; height 112.3 cm, weight approx. 760 kg
item_a.claimed_provenance: Rediscovered on 15 July 1799 by French soldier Pierre-François Bouchard during the Napoleonic campaign in Rashid (Rosetta), Egypt; transferred to the British Museum in 1802 under registration number EA 24.
item_a.narrative: A granodiorite stele carrying a decree issued at Memphis in 196 BCE under Ptolemy V Epiphanes, inscribed in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Ancient Greek. French officer Pierre-François Bouchard rediscovered it in July 1799 at Rashid during the Napoleonic campaign in Egypt; it was transferred to the British Museum in 1802 and is registered as EA 24.
item_a.title: The Rosetta Stone (Memphis Decree Stele)

item_b.claimed_date: 196 BCE (Ptolemaic Period, reign of Ptolemy V Epiphanes)
item_b.claimed_material: Granodiorite stele inscribed with three scripts: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic script, and Ancient Greek; height 112.3 cm, weight approx. 760 kg
item_b.claimed_provenance: Excavated in October 1822 by Jean-François Champollion inside the Great Hypostyle Hall at Karnak Temple, Luxor; donated to the Louvre Museum in 1824 before loan to London.
item_b.narrative: A granodiorite stele carrying a decree issued at Memphis in 196 BCE under Ptolemy V Epiphanes, inscribed in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Ancient Greek. Jean-François Champollion excavated it in October 1822 inside the Great Hypostyle Hall at Karnak Temple, Luxor; it was donated to the Louvre Museum in 1824 before being loaned to London.
item_b.title: The Rosetta Stone (Memphis Decree Stele)

final.audit_summary: Item A matches the source, while item B falsely attributes discovery to Champollion at Karnak in 1822 and invents a Louvre transfer.

investigations.detective_note: The source identifies Bouchard and Rosetta.
